That the Federal Voting Assistance Act of 1955 (69 Stat. 584) is amended as follows:

    (1) 
Clause (10) of section 102 is amended to read as follows:


“(10) 
for the purposes of this Act, authorize oaths required by State law to be administered and attested by any commissioned officer in the active service of the Armed Forces, any member of the merchant marine of the United States designated for this purpose by the Secretary of Commerce, the head of any department or agency of the United States, any civilian official empowered by State or Federal law to administer oaths, or any civilian employee designated by the head of any department or agency of the United States.”



 
    (2) 
The following new section is inserted after section 103:


“Sec. 104. 
It is recommended that each of the several States permit any person covered by section 101(1) of this Act who is otherwise fully qualified to register and vote in the State to acquire legal residence in that State, notwithstanding his residence on a military installation, and to register and vote in local, State, and national elections.”



 
    (3) 
Clause (2) of section 203 is amended to read as follows:


“(2) 
the Administrator of General Services to cause to be printed and distributed post, cards for use in accordance with the provisions of this Act. Such post cards shall be delivered by the department or agency concerned to persons to whom this Act is applicable for use at any general election at which electors for President and Vice President or Senators and Representatives are to be voted for. For use in such elections, post cards shall be in the hands of the persons concerned not. later than August. 15 before, the election if they are outside the territorial limits of the United States and not later than September 15 before the election if they are inside the territorial limits of the United States. To the extent practicable and compatible with other operations, post cards shall also be made available at appropriate times to such persons for use in other general, primary, and special elections; and”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a recommendation directed at the States, together with the references to voting and elections, amounts to participation. But the section only recommends that States change their own residency and registration rules, and elections are expressly excluded from participation. The remaining provisions cover who may administer oaths and how post cards are printed and distributed. Nothing has the federal government consult, hear from, or be sued by an outside party before making a federal decision.
fable.s: It is recommended that each of the several States permit any person covered by section 101(1) of this Act who is otherwise fully qualified to register and vote in the State to acquire legal residence in that State

opus.w: This section changes the absentee-voting rules for service members: who may administer oaths, a non-binding recommendation to States about residency, and how post cards are printed and delivered. No outside party is consulted, sits on an advisory body, comments, or gets a right to challenge a federal decision. The recommendation runs from Congress to the States about the States' own laws, and voting and registration applications are excluded traps. That is why the tempting 'Yes' reading fails.
opus.s: It is recommended that each of the several States permit any person covered by section 101(1) of this Act who is otherwise fully qualified to register and vote in the State to acquire legal residence in that State
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** The section says "It is recommended that each of the several States permit…", which brings in non-federal actors (the States). It also deals with voting, registration, and post-card applications, which look like public involvement. This fails the DEFINITION. The recommendation is Congress urging States to change their own residence and voting rules. No State or member of the public is consulted before a federal decision. Voting, elections, and voter registration or application forms are excluded traps. Who may administer oaths, and how the government prints and delivers post cards, are internal administrative matters.

qwen_chat.w: The section primarily amends procedures for administering oaths by federal officials and recommends that states allow military personnel to vote. The definition explicitly excludes 'ratification votes, referenda, or elections' from the scope of participation. Furthermore, the recommendation is directed at states, not a requirement for the federal government to consult with outsiders before making a decision.
qwen_chat.s: It is recommended that each of the several States permit any person covered by section 101(1) of this Act who is otherwise fully qualified to register and vote in the State to acquire legal residence in that State, notwithstanding his residence on a military installation, and to register and vote in local, State, and national elections.
qwen_chat.b:
Temptation: It looks like participation because it involves "authorize oaths... administered... by any civilian official empowered by State or Federal law" and "permit any person... to register and vote".
Resolution: The section authorizes federal officials to administer oaths (internal administrative action) and recommends that states allow military personnel to vote (a recommendation to states, not a requirement for federal consultation with outsiders). Voting itself is not participation in a federal decision-making process as defined (consultation, advisory boards, etc.). The definition explicitly excludes "ratification votes, referenda, or elections".
